headline: Vance says the war lost it. Trump: I'd do it again.
summary: Vice President Vance posted 600 words on X on Wednesday: "The reason we lost is the war." Trump agreed the Iran war "largely" decided the midterms, then said he would do it again, because Iran cannot have a nuclear weapon. The US and Israel attacked Tehran in February. Oil fell about $8 a barrel on the day.

cover_question.q: Did Vance just turn on Trump?

cover_answer: Halfway. Trump called it fine and says he'd do it again.
table_question: If your team loses, should the captain say whose fault it was?

5-7.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
5-7.script: The country had a big vote on Tuesday, and the president's team lost a lot of seats. His helper, the vice president, said the reason was the war with Iran. Lots of people didn't want it, and gas cost more. Like a coach saying out loud which play lost the game. The grown-ups are sorting it out.
5-7.why: A coach naming the bad play is something they have seen. Keep the war itself to one line; the vote is the story here.
5-7.why_long: A child this age reasons from what is in front of them, so the script turns a 600-word post into a coach naming the play that lost the game, and keeps the war to one line: people didn't want it, and gas cost more. Expect "is the war over now?" No. The president says he will end it when it is done right.

8-12.script: In February the US and Israel attacked Iran. Gas got expensive, and on Tuesday many 2024 Trump voters picked Democrats. Vance wrote that chain out: the war cost the election. Trump agreed, then said he'd do it again. An election is a report card every two years. This one got read out loud.
8-12.why: A chain they can follow: war, gas prices, votes. They want to know if the people in charge admit it.
8-12.why_long: This age is learning cause and effect and whether adults own their mistakes, so the script hands them the chain Vance wrote out: war in February, gas prices up, 2024 Trump voters picking Democrats. The report card is a mechanism they live with. Expect "does Vance get in trouble?" No. Trump called it fine.

13-17.script: Vance never named Trump, but wrote that anyone who thinks the war was worth losing the Senate for six years should say so. Honesty or ambition? Second: Trump says the war "largely" lost the election and he'd do it again, because Iran can't have a bomb. Can a leader be right and still deserve to lose?
13-17.why: Two true things: Vance broke ranks and Trump let him. At this age they can hold both and will tell you which one matters.
13-17.why_long: A teenager can hold two true things at once: the vice president broke with the president in public over the war, and the president called the post fine and says he would do it again. The script asks whether honesty and ambition can be one move. Expect "so who's right?" Say what you think. They're testing.

5-7.a: No. The president says he'll end it when it's done right.

8-12.q: Why would a war change how people vote?
8-12.a: Gas cost more and many didn't want the war. They switched.

8-12.q: Does Vance get in trouble for saying that?
8-12.a: No. Trump read the post and said it was fine.

13-17.q: Did Vance just turn on Trump?
13-17.a: Halfway. He never named Trump, and Trump called the post fine.

13-17.q: Would Trump really do it again?
13-17.a: He says so: no choice, Iran can't have a nuclear weapon.
